questions.stem: What does CDC stand for in data processing?
options: Central Data Catalogue
Change Data Capture
Continuous Data Copy
Controlled Data Cache
Consolidated Data Centre
questions.explanation: CDC is Change Data Capture: the moment data changes in a database, only the changed data is picked up and pushed to the next layer.

questions.stem: What does a CDC process pick up and push to the next layer?
options: The whole table every time
Only the table metadata
A random sample of rows
Only the data that has changed
Only rows older than a day
questions.explanation: With CDC, only the changed data is picked up, whether a new row, an updated row or a deleted row.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the kinds of change that CDC captures?
options: A table being re-indexed
A new row being added
An existing row being updated
A previously added row being deleted
None of these; all are captured
questions.explanation: Changed data means a new row, an updated row or a deleted row; re-indexing is not a data change.

questions.stem: Why is CDC mostly not run in Real-Time even though it could be?
options: Because databases forbid real-time reads
Because CDC only works in overnight batches
Because Real-Time plus CDC needs a lot of memory processing, which carries a heavy TCO, so it depends on the ROI of the business case
Because transaction logs are only written daily
Because real-time data has no previous state
questions.explanation: Real-Time combined with CDC needs heavy memory processing with heavy total cost of ownership, so whether to do it depends on return on investment.

questions.stem: Which CDC method is described as the slowest and requiring the heaviest processing?
options: Reading the transaction log
Using date columns in source tables
Capturing changes at the application level
Streaming from CCTV
Keeping the previous dataset in one table, loading the new dataset in another and comparing them
questions.explanation: Comparing a previous and a new copy of the data to find deleted, new or changed rows is the slowest method and needs the heaviest processing.

questions.stem: Which CDC method is recommended and most commonly used?
options: Comparing two full copies of the table
Using date columns in every source table
Reading the transaction log generated by insert, update and delete operations
Capturing changes at the application level
Polling the source tables every second
questions.explanation: Reading the transaction log instead of hitting the source tables has no impact on the source database and only minimal I/O impact, so it is the recommended and mostly used approach.

questions.stem: What is the drawback of the CDC method that relies on date columns in source tables?
options: It requires the source data model to have date fields in each table, which may need extensive development effort, and it has a processing impact on the source
It cannot detect deleted rows
It only works with transaction logs
It is the most recent method and few solutions support it
It requires an in-memory database
questions.explanation: Using date columns is easy, but if the source lacks date fields in each table it needs extensive backend and frontend development, and it also affects source performance.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the application-level CDC method?
options: It compares two snapshots of each table
It is the oldest and most widely adopted method
It relies on date columns in the source
It has a heavy impact on source I/O
It is the most recent method, used by very few solutions, in which the application pushes each write for CDC processing with no impact on the database or I/O
questions.explanation: In the application-level method the application pushes the operation for CDC processing as it writes to the database, with no impact on the source database or I/O; it is the most recent and least used method.

questions.stem: Why does the pipeline carrying a Facebook LIKE downstream have nothing to do with CDC?
options: Because Facebook does not use databases
Because it always appends from the application level rather than capturing a change to a previous state
Because LIKE data is processed in batches
Because CDC only applies to deletions
Because CDC is only used in data warehouses
questions.explanation: Real-Time pipelines such as a LIKE or live CCTV streaming append new data from the application level; CDC applies only when the previous state of data changes.

questions.stem: What must organisations planning for Real-Time processing evaluate?
options: Which BI tool to buy
How many batches to run per day
Whether to switch to a NoSQL database
Whether CDC is required at all
Whether to disable transaction logs
questions.explanation: Because Real-Time and CDC are different topics, organisations planning for Real-Time must evaluate whether CDC is required or not.
